cells.tense: The fairness is running now, and both hands are on it.
cells.ask: Say the number out loud before either of you moves: what you gave, what you're owed, what you'll call even.
cells.core:
You're keeping the exchange honest and you can feel it working. Not counting favors under your breath — you give what you give and you take what comes without making either one a debt. What lands between you lands level, and people can rest on it.

One thing to watch. Keeping it level has become part of your job now, the way you hold the room's arrangements. So when an imbalance shows up, say the number out loud and let it close. Earning your keep is different from being told you're keeping score. The fairness came from you before there was anything to protect.

cells.tense: You're pricing the next thing before it's been handed to you.
cells.ask: Do one thing for someone this week and don't track it. No tally, no nod to the score.
cells.core:
You're bracing for what you'll owe before anything's been offered. Someone reaches out and you've already worked out the return, the cost, the condition — the exchange hasn't happened and it's already been settled. That kind of vigilance looks like fairness and quietly runs on fear.

Underneath it, the steadier move is there: staying level while a real imbalance works itself through. So stop doing the math ahead of the moment. Give once this week without entering it anywhere. The room doesn't need to see you absorb the cost, and neither does the person. Standing firm isn't the same as standing first.

cells.tense: The arrangement in front of you went stale, and you're still sitting in it.
cells.ask: Look at one exchange you let go on too long. Then either set a new term or walk away from it exactly once.
cells.core:
You stopped being in the exchange. Things go one way for a while, favorable or not, and you let it keep going rather than touch it — and the longer it runs, the harder it is to reach in. Staying quiet has started to look like principle. It isn't. It's a door you've already passed.

What sharpens this is small attention. Pick one relationship where the terms drifted and look at it closely. Then say the new term out loud, or end it clean, once. Not to fix the other person, and not to be fair for show — to see what you actually want to offer before you offer it.
cells.sheetLine: You're letting an old trade run itself out.

cells.tense: You're reworking the terms while alive and treating it as just the way it's kept.
cells.ask: Name one standing arrangement you keep running in the room, and say whose it is when it comes up next.
cells.core:
You shape how people share — what gets given, what gets handed back, who gets a pass and who doesn't. It happens in the way you talk and what you let slide, and you'd call that just being around. The steering is real. The saying-so isn't.

That rule you're using — you can feel it land when the moment comes. Say it, even once, and let the room hear it as yours. Drop the neutral pose in that one spot. You'll still be able to feel out what's fair without the quiet refusal that you decided anything. The decision was yours to sign.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the arrangements. You call it being around.
